status.en: 9 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 50% fewer than the week before, most of them in Baghdad, Kirkuk and Erbil.
status.nb: 9 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 50 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Baghdad, Kirkuk og Erbil.

summary.en: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi has assumed direct control of Iraq's intelligence service while Iran intensifies pressure over militia activities and PJAK presence. Baghdad and Damascus advanced talks on the Sharaa pipeline, border security and oil exports, and the Iraqi government signed a gas capture agreement with US firm Morgan Hughes. Security forces dismantled a drug-trafficking network, arresting 31 suspects, and Erbil police detained four suspects in connection with a woman's murder, while the PMF denied having paid Iranian advisers. A memorial was unveiled in Erbil for victims of the 2024 Iranian missile attack.
summary.nb: Statsminister Al-Zaidi har tatt direkte kontroll over Iraks etterretningstjeneste mens Iran intensiverer presset over militsaktivitetene og PJAK-tilstedeværelsen. Bagdad og Damaskus har fremmet samtaler om Sharaa-rørledningen, grensesikkerhet og oljeeksport, og den irakiske regjeringen har signert en gassinnsamlingsavtale med det amerikanske firmaet Morgan Hughes. Sikkerhetsstyrker har demontert et narkotikasmuglingsnettverk og arrestert 31 mistenkte, og politiet i Erbil har pågrepet fire mistenkte i forbindelse med drapet på en kvinne, mens PMF har benektet å ha betalt iranske rådgivere. Et minnesmerke ble avduket i Erbil for ofrene for det iranske missilangrepet i 2024.

background.title: Iraqi conflict
background.extract: The Iraqi conflict is a series of violent events that began with the 2003 American-led invasion of Iraq and deposition of Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein, followed by a series of conflicts including the protracted Iraq War (2003–2011), the Iraqi insurgency (2011–2013), the War in Iraq (2013–2017), and most recently, the small-scale Islamic State insurgency in 4 provinces located in Northern Iraq since 2017.
